checked.claim: Amendment dated 10 March 2026, main provisions in force 11 September 2026, up to 10% in aggravated cases
checked.evidence: IAPP: promulgated 10 March 2026, takes effect 11 September 2026, 10% turnover ceiling. Digital Today: revised March 2026, effective 11 September 2026. DLA Piper: effective 11 September 2026, 3% to 10% in specific circumstances.

checked.claim: 3% cap since 15 September 2023; 10% from 11 September 2026 for repeat wilful or grossly negligent violations within three years, 10 million or more data subjects, or failure to comply with a corrective order
checked.evidence: DLA Piper: 'raised from 3% to 10% of total revenue in specific circumstances, including: repeated violations involving willful misconduct or gross negligence within a three-year period; violations affecting 10 million or more data subjects; or failure to comply with a corrective order'. The KRW 2 billion no-turnover cap was not shown in sources fetched; consistent with my understanding of Art 64-2 and already hedged.

checked.claim: June 2026, reportedly about KRW 624 billion, insider breach affecting about 34 million accounts and unlawful collection; Coupang to challenge
checked.evidence: Korea Herald and UPI: decision 11 June 2026; total KRW 624.7 billion = KRW 423.6 billion for the breach (about 37.5 million users: 33.2 million members and 4.3 million others) + KRW 201.2 billion for collecting activity records of 11.17 million users without authorisation + KRW 248 million on Coupang Fulfillment Services. Breach by a former engineer misusing a signing key. Coupang said it would 'clarify the facts through legal procedures'. Kakao KRW 15.1 billion was in 2024 (Korea Herald SKT article: 'last year').
checked.replacement: On 11 June 2026 the PIPC imposed a record KRW 624.7 billion on Coupang: KRW 423.6 billion for an insider breach by a former engineer affecting about 37.5 million users, KRW 201.2 billion for collecting 11.17 million users' activity on other apps and websites without authorisation, and KRW 248 million on a subsidiary. Coupang said it would contest the decision through legal procedures. Earlier comparators include Kakao (KRW 15.1 billion, 2024).

checked.evidence: CPO Magazine gives a different date (15 June) and wrongly places the SK Telecom fine in 2026; a primary-press source is better.

notes: Most serious problem: the Coupang case was soft and partly wrong (date given only as June, 'reportedly', about 34 million accounts). Primary press gives 11 June 2026, KRW 624.7 billion split into breach and unlawful-collection surcharges, about 37.5 million users.
